To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have studied the effect of pressure on optical properties of semimagnetic seminconductors ZnFeSe, we have observed that absorption edge of ZnFeSe has two components, and that the second component, related to presence of Fe2+ ions, is weakly dependent on pressure and temperature.

the optical absorption edge of ZnFeSe can be considered as two components: the first one is the fundamental absorption edge which is strongly dependent on temperature and pressure, the second one is related to the presence of iron and is weakly dependent on pressure and temperature and can be assigned to charge transfer Fe2+- to Fe1+- or Fe2+ - to Fe3+.
the optical absorption edges of mixed crystals Zn1-xFexe (0.01 < x < 0.05) can be considered as sum of two components, the fundamental absorption edge and absorption related to the presence of iron.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the optical absorption edges of the Zn1-xFexe mixed crystals under high pressure.
optical absorption of Zn1-xFexe crystals in a wide range of iron concentration and pressure.
the optical properties of Zn1-xFexe mixed crystals in the temperature and pressure range of 77-300 K and up to 2 GPa.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the absorption edges of Zn1-xFexe semimagnetic semicoductors can be considered to be a sum of two contributions, namely, the intrinsic fundamental absorption edge of the host ZnSe semiconductor, and the extra absorption due to the presence of iron.

the absorption edges in Zn1-xFexe are determined by the Fe2+-Fe3+ and Fe3+-Fe3+ transition, and that the pressure dependence of the absorption edge is governed by the change in the band gap of the host semiconductor.

the anomalous pressure dependence of the absorption edge is a consequence of the existence of the charge transfer Fe3+/Fe2+ and/or Fe2+/Fe1+, and that these transitions are not related to the fundamental band gap.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fundamental edge of the absorption of ZnFeFeSe is a typical semimagnetic semiconductor.

the pressure dependence of the fundamental absorption edge is similar to the pressure dependence of absorption edge in Zn1-xCdxSe, while the extra component of absorption in ZnFeSe is different from the extra component in ZnCdSe.

the fundamental absorption edge is shifted toward the high-energy side with the increase of the pressure, and the pressure dependence of the fundamental band gap is well fitted by a quadratic function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the absorption edge is not a single absorption edge, but a sum of two absorption edges, one of which is due to the presence of iron.
the absorption edge of ZnFeSe has a very strong pressure dependence and can be used to measure the pressure.
the pressure dependence of the absorption edges of Zn1-xFexe can be considered as the sum of two components.
